meta.title: Vocabulary Automator – Anki cards from any text
meta.description: Select a word in any app, press a hotkey, check the card and add it to Anki. With translation, pronunciation and language recognition. For macOS.
meta.ogDescription: Select a word anywhere, press your hotkey, approve the card. It lands in Anki.
meta.ogImageAlt: The Vocabulary Automator approval window with a card for the word “reluctant”

hero.title: Turn the words you read into Anki cards.
hero.subline_html: Select a word or phrase in any app and press <kbd>⇧⌘C</kbd> (Shift-Command-C). Vocabulary Automator looks up the translation and the pronunciation and shows you the finished card. Press <kbd>Enter</kbd>, and it is in your deck.
hero.meta: Version {version} · Preview · Apple Silicon and Intel
hero.metaFallback: The macOS download is not available yet.
hero.note: Windows and Linux follow with the first official release.
hero.mobileNote: Vocabulary Automator is a desktop app. Open this page on your Mac to download it.

mock.label: Illustration of the approval window
mock.description: The approval window with a card for the English word “reluctant”: the language chips “English” (selected) and “French”, “→ German”, the deck “English”, the note type “Vocabulary”, the back “widerwillig”, an example sentence with its German translation, a button that plays the pronunciation and the buttons “Discard” and “Add to Anki”.
mock.title: New card
mock.exampleValue: He was reluctant to admit his mistake.
mock.exampleTargetValue: Er gab seinen Fehler nur widerwillig zu.
mock.hint: Enter adds the card, Esc discards it, Shift+Enter starts a new line.

s1.title: Select and press the hotkey
s1.body_html: Select a word or phrase in any app you can copy text from and press ⇧⌘CShift-Command-C. The app copies the selection and then puts your previous clipboard text back.

s2.title: The card fills itself in
s2.body: The app recognizes which of your languages the text is in, translates it and adds the pronunciation. English words also get an example sentence. Chinese gets pinyin and the HSK level.

s3.title: You check it
s3.body_html: The approval window shows the card. Change whatever you like, then press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to add it or <kbd>Esc</kbd> to discard it.

s4.title: It lands in Anki
s4.body: The card is saved to the local history and sent through AnkiConnect to the deck of its language, with a reverse card (on by default except for Chinese; it can be switched off per language). If Anki is closed, the card waits in the history until you sync it.

f1.title: Works in any app you can copy from
f1.body: One global hotkey, wherever you read. Close the settings window and the app keeps running in the menu bar, with the hotkey still active.

f2.title: You approve every card
f2.body: Nothing goes to Anki until you press “Add to Anki”. Every field can be edited first, and the pronunciation is recorded again if you change the word.

f3.title: Recognizes your languages
f3.body: Under “My languages”, list what you learn: English, German, French, Spanish, Italian or Chinese. The hotkey recognizes which one the text is in, without an internet connection. If a short word such as “message” could be English or French, the window marks its guess, and one click switches the language.
f3.visualLabel: Illustration: the language chips “English?” and “French” next to “→ German”, with the hint shown when the language is unsure
f3.hint: This could be more than one of your languages. It was read as English. If that is wrong, choose the right language: translation, example, pronunciation and deck are fetched again.

f4.title: Every language in its own deck
f4.body: Each language has its own deck, note type and reverse-card setting. Fields are matched by their names: “Audio” gets the pronunciation, “English Sentence” the English example.

f5.title: Warns before anything gets lost
f5.body: Before you approve, the window lists every value the note type would drop, such as audio without a matching field. If a service fails, the card is still created, a warning says what is missing, and you can type it in yourself.
f5.visualLabel: Illustration: the warning “Not everything would reach Anki” for a pronunciation without a field
f5.lostItem: Pronunciation: no field of “Basic” is chosen for the audio.

f6.title: Chinese with pinyin and HSK level
f6.body: Text with Chinese characters is always captured as Chinese. Pinyin with tone marks and the HSK 3.0 level come from a bundled list of 10,969 words. Words outside the list still get pinyin.
f6.visualLabel: Illustration: the word 银行 with the pinyin yín háng and the level HSK 2

f7.title: Works when Anki is closed
f7.body: Every approved card is saved to a local history first. If Anki is not running, the card stays there as “Not in Anki yet”, and “Sync pending to Anki” sends it later.

f8.title: Rare words flagged
f8.body: A single English word that is rare gets a note saying so, with a more common synonym when Datamuse knows one.

f9.title: More hotkeys, more language pairs
f9.body: Hotkey profiles add shortcuts with a fixed language pair and, if you like, a deck of their own.

f10.title: Anki setup included
f10.body: If Anki or the AnkiConnect add-on is missing, the app can install it, but only after you agree in a dialog that says what is downloaded, from where and how it is checked. Both downloads are pinned to a fixed version and verified by SHA-256 before anything is installed.

data.title: What happens to your data
data.intro: Vocabulary Automator has no account and no server of its own. Your cards, your history and your settings stay on your Mac. To fill in a card, the app sends the captured text to the services in this table. Apart from these requests, nothing leaves your Mac.
data.caption: Requests the app sends, and when

r1.what: The captured text and the language pair, plus your contact e-mail if you entered one

r2.what: The captured text and its language
r2.when: Every capture, for the pronunciation. Again when you approve a card whose word you changed

r3.when: When a reverse card is also sent to Anki, for its pronunciation

r4.when: English captures, for an example sentence

r5.when: Single English words, for the rarity check and a synonym

r6.what: The example sentence and the language pair, plus your contact e-mail if you entered one
r6.when: When a card has an example sentence, for its translation

r7.what: A request for the newest version number, with no captured text
r7.when: About 10 seconds after the settings window opens

r8.what: Download requests for Anki or AnkiConnect
r8.when: Only when you install them from the app and agree

n1.title: Stays on your Mac:
n1.body: language recognition, pinyin and HSK level, your history and your settings. AnkiConnect also runs on your Mac (127.0.0.1).

n2.title: Switching the language:
n2.body: when you choose another language in the approval window, the card is fetched again, with the same requests.

n3.title: Please do not capture passwords or other private text.
n3.body: Everything you capture goes to the services above.

n4.title: Where your data lives:
n4.body_html: the history is in ~/Library/Application Support/VocabularyAutomator/vocab.sqlite3, the settings are in ~/Library/Application Support/com.ankiautomator.app/config.json, and the app’s log is in ~/Library/Logs/com.ankiautomator.app.

i1.title: A Mac
i1.body: With Apple Silicon or Intel. Vocabulary Automator is developed on macOS 26 Tahoe. Older macOS versions have not been tested yet.

i2.body_html: With the AnkiConnect add-on (code 2055492159). Cards reach Anki while it is open; otherwise they wait in the history. The app can install both for you.

i3.title: The Accessibility permission
i3.body_html: So the hotkey can copy your selection. The steps are below.

i4.title: An internet connection
i4.body: For translation, pronunciation and example sentences.

download.title: Download & install
download.macMeta: Disk image (.dmg) · Apple Silicon and Intel
download.macFallback: The macOS download is not available yet.
download.checksumHelp_html: To check the file, run shasum -a 256 ~/Downloads/{dmgFile} in Terminal and compare the result with the value above.
download.otherBody: Versions for Windows and Linux will be available with the first official release on GitHub Releases. There is no date yet.
download.previewBody: This is a preview build. Apple has not notarized it, because the project does not have an Apple Developer ID yet. That is why macOS warns you the first time you open it. The steps below take you past that warning and set up the one permission the app needs.

s1.title: Install
s1.body: Open the downloaded .dmg and drag Vocabulary Automator into the Applications folder.

s2.title: Open it for the first time
s2.sequoia_html: macOS 15 Sequoia and later: Double-click Vocabulary Automator in Applications. macOS says it could not verify the app. Click Done. Open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll down to Security and click Open Anyway next to the message about Vocabulary Automator. Confirm with Open Anyway and your password or Touch ID.
s2.sonoma_html: macOS 14 Sonoma and earlier: Control-click Vocabulary Automator in Applications, choose Open, then click Open in the dialog.
s2.once: You need to do this only once per version.

s3.title: Let the hotkey copy text
s3.body_html: The hotkey copies your selection with a simulated ⌘CCommand-C, which macOS allows only with the Accessibility permission. The app does not ask for it by itself. Open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility, click +, choose Vocabulary Automator in Applications and turn its switch on. If the settings window is open, it shows a short message that points here. If the hotkey seems to do nothing, check this permission first. If a capture still copies nothing, quit the app (menu bar icon > Quit) and open it again.

s4.title: Connect Anki
s4.body_html: In Vocabulary Automator, open the “Anki connection” tab. It shows what is missing and, if you agree, installs Anki or AnkiConnect for you. After installing AnkiConnect, restart Anki, and keep it open while you capture. The app’s language (English or German) is set at the top right of the settings window.

s5.title: Add your languages
s5.body_html: On “My languages”, add each language you learn and choose its deck and note type. A deck that does not exist yet is created with the first card. Your own language, the one cards are translated into, is set on “Capture & Language”.

s6.title: Try it
s6.body_html: Select a word anywhere and press ⇧⌘CShift-Command-C. Or type a word under “Try a capture” on the “Capture & Language” tab.

download.updateBody_html: The preview does not update itself. To update, download the new version from this page, quit Vocabulary Automator (menu bar icon > Quit) and replace the app in Applications. Your settings and history are kept. macOS may show the warning from step 2 again. macOS also treats each new preview build as a different app, so open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility, remove the old Vocabulary Automator entry with − and add the new one with +. If the app shows “Version … is available – restart to update”, its button cannot install the preview: download the new version from this page instead.
download.knowTitle: Good to know before you install
download.k1: Example sentences exist for English so far. Chinese cards get a simple template sentence, and French, German, Spanish and Italian cards get none yet.
download.k2: Translations come from a free translation service. Check them before you approve.
download.k3: Captures are limited to 100 characters, and you can raise that to 500 in the settings.
download.k4: The app only adds new cards to Anki. It never changes or deletes your existing notes.
download.k5: The preview is not notarized and does not update itself.

q1.a_html: Nothing. The preview is a free download, and the services it uses for translation, pronunciation and example sentences work without an account or payment.

q2.a_html: Anki is a free flashcard program that shows each card again shortly before you would forget it. Vocabulary Automator adds the cards; you review them in Anki.

q3.q: Do I need an account or an API key?
q3.a_html: No. The translation service, MyMemory, works without a key. MyMemory allows about 5,000 characters a day anonymously. If you add a contact e-mail under “Capture & Language”, it allows about 50,000. The address goes to MyMemory only.

q4.q: Why does macOS warn me when I open the app?
q4.a_html: The preview build is not notarized by Apple yet, so macOS cannot verify it. Follow step 2 under “Download & install” once, and the app opens normally from then on.

q5.q: Why does the app need the Accessibility permission?
q5.a_html: To copy your selection, the hotkey sends ⌘CCommand-C to the app you are reading in, and macOS allows that only with the Accessibility permission. Vocabulary Automator uses it for nothing else.

q6.q: What happens if Anki is closed?
q6.a_html: The card is saved to the history anyway and marked “Not in Anki yet”. Once Anki is running again, click “Sync pending to Anki” on the History tab.

q7.q: Does it work without an internet connection?
q7.a_html: Partly. Language recognition, pinyin and the HSK level work offline. Without a connection, the translation, the example’s translation and the pronunciation stay empty (English and Chinese cards still get a template example sentence), a warning says so, and you can type the values in yourself.

q8.a_html: English, German, French, Spanish, Italian and Chinese (Simplified), in any pair. The hotkey recognizes the language among those you list under “My languages”. For other text it uses the source language set on “Capture & Language”.

q9.q: Which note type should I use?
q9.a_html: Any note type you already have in Anki. You choose one per language, and its fields are matched by their names, or you assign them yourself. The approval window warns you when a value has no field. For Chinese, use a note type with Hanzi, Pinyin, Meaning and Audio fields together with the Chinese preset.

q10.a_html: The hotkey copies the selection through the clipboard and then puts your previous text back. Only text can be restored: an image on the clipboard is replaced. The restored text also loses the marker that password managers use to keep a copied password out of clipboard history.

q11.a_html: Yes, on the “Capture & Language” tab. Type the shortcut as modifiers and one key joined by “+”, for example CommandOrControl+Shift+C. It needs Cmd, Ctrl or Alt (Option); only function keys (F1–F24) may stand alone. Hotkey profiles add more shortcuts, each with its own language pair and deck.

q12.a_html: Quit the app (menu bar icon > Quit) and move it from Applications to the Trash. Remove its entry under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility. To delete your history, settings and log as well, delete the folders VocabularyAutomator and com.ankiautomator.app in ~/Library/Application Support and the folder ~/Library/Logs/com.ankiautomator.app. Finder hides ~/Library: choose Go > Go to Folder and enter the path. Cards already in Anki stay there.

footer.independence: Vocabulary Automator is an independent project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anki, AnkiWeb or the AnkiConnect add-on.
footer.credits: For Chinese, the app bundles data from CC-CEDICT (CC BY-SA 4.0) and two HSK word lists (MIT License). The full credits are in the app’s help dialog.
footer.siteNote: This website sets no cookies, uses no analytics and loads nothing from other servers.
